messages:
Mira Chen: Quick q — our Go SDK returns a typed RateLimitError for 429 with RetryAfter, but the JS SDK surfaces a generic HttpError (just status + message). This is breaking sample-app retry logic: Go code does exponential backoff, JS just fails fast. Anyone run into parity pain here?
Alejandra Rivera: Yep seen that. Customers hit flaky retry behavior when they mix SDKs in a polyglot stack.
Kevin Lowe: Is this just 429 or other codes too? 503 shows up in infra, 499 shows up from nginx (client closed) which is ambiguous.
Mira Chen: Mostly 429/503 right now. 499 is confusing — some apps interpret it as a transient and retry which causes duplicate ops.
Samir Patel: Proposal: unify around a small typed error contract across SDKs: {code: string, http_status: int, retryable: bool, retry_after_ms?: int, transient_hint?: string}. Keep it minimal.
Chloe Park: Love minimal. Also need clear docs/example for how to handle 499 specifically (don't retry by default).
devex-bot: Suggested link: https://redwood.dev/internal/error-contracts (internal) :link: (stub)
Alejandra Rivera: Implementation notes — Go already returns structured type. For JS/TS we should return a class with properties and exported type guards so TS users can narrow. e.g., `if (err.retryable) { await backoff.retry(...) }`
Kevin Lowe: What about mapping HTTP -> code? Right now some SDKs put code = "rate_limited", others use "http_429". We should standardize stable codes (snake_case) we can document.
Samir Patel: Agreed: stable canonical codes (rate_limited, service_unavailable, auth_required, bad_request, client_abort). Keep mapping table in repo.
Mira Chen: Also add guidance for streaming endpoints — partial responses can surface different error shapes. Need consistency there too.
Chloe Park: UX detail: include human_readable_hint on the typed error for onboarding (1–2 sentence). e.g., "quota exceeded; retry after 12s or talk to infra". Helps support and sample apps.
Alejandra Rivera: For sample-apps: update handler wrappers to check `err.retryable` and prefer `err.retry_after_ms` if present. Add examples for both auto-retry (idempotent only) and fail-fast (non-idempotent).
Samir Patel: I'll open a RFC PR with the proposed shape + mapping table. Also will add a unit test harness that validates JS/Go/py errors emit the same serialized fields over the wire.
Kevin Lowe: One more gotcha: SDKs that wrap lower-level HTTP libs sometimes lose headers (Retry-After). Make sure we parse `Retry-After` into retry_after_ms.
Mira Chen: Good call. Also call out proxies returning 499 — default policy: treat 499 as non-retry unless we can detect client disconnect vs upstream cancel. Add a flag `client_aborted` if we detect it.
Chloe Park: Can we add a tiny sample snippet in the onboarding quickstart for retries? That reduces support tickets.
Samir Patel: Yes — sample code: ```js
// JS retry example
try { await client.generate(...) } catch (err) {
  if (err.retryable && idempotent) {
    await backoff.retry(() => client.generate(...), {delay: err.retry_after_ms || 1000})
  } else {
    throw err
  }
}
```
Alejandra Rivera: I'll sync with docs to add the mapping table + quickstart snippet.
Mira Chen: Action items: Samir PR for RFC + tests, Alejandra docs + sample apps update, Kevin audit HTTP header passthrough in Go runtime, Chloe add onboarding snippet. I'll open a follow-up thread for streaming-specific shapes. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: Opening PR in ~30m.
Kevin Lowe: I'll run a quick grep for `Retry-After` usage across services and file issues.
Chloe Park: Adding a small onboarding ticket now.
Mira Chen: Thanks team — this should reduce noisy support signals and make SDK behavior predictable across languages.
